title: ഒന്നാം പ്രധാന ശിലാശാസനം: മൃഗബലിയും രാജകീയ അടുക്കളയും
excerpt: അശോകൻ മൃഗബലി നിയന്ത്രിക്കുകയും രാജകീയ അടുക്കളയിൽ മൃഗങ്ങളെ കൊല്ലുന്നത് ഗണ്യമായി കുറഞ്ഞതായി പറയുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.

thumbnail.alt: ഹുൾറ്റ്ഷിന്റെ 1925-ലെ പതിപ്പിലെ ഗിർനാറിലെ ബ്രാഹ്മി ലിപിയിലുള്ള ശാസനത്തിന്റെ പകർപ്പ്

title: 15,000 വർഷം മുമ്പ് പൂമ്പുഹാറിന് കടലിൽ ഒരു തുറമുഖമുണ്ടായിരുന്നോ?
excerpt: സോണാർ സർവേകൾ ബംഗാൾ ഉൾക്കടലിന്റെ അടിത്തട്ടിൽ തുറമുഖം പോലുള്ള രൂപങ്ങൾ കണ്ടെത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. എന്നാൽ അവ 15,000 വർഷം പഴക്കമുള്ള തുറമുഖമാണെന്ന അവകാശവാദം ഇനിയും തെളിയിച്ചിട്ടില്ല.

thumbnail.alt: ബംഗാൾ ഉൾക്കടലിന്റെ തീരത്തുള്ള പൂമ്പുഹാറിന്റെ വിശാല മണൽക്കടപ്പുറത്ത് കയറ്റിവെച്ച മത്സ്യബന്ധന വള്ളങ്ങൾ

title: അത്തിരമ്പാക്കത്തെ പത്തു ലക്ഷം വർഷത്തിലേറെ പഴക്കമുള്ള ശിലായുധങ്ങൾ
excerpt: ചെന്നൈയ്ക്കടുത്ത് മണ്ണിനടിയിൽ കിടന്നിരുന്ന അഷ്യൂലിയൻ കൈക്കോടാലികൾ, ദക്ഷിണേന്ത്യയിൽ കുറഞ്ഞത് 10.7 ലക്ഷം വർഷം മുമ്പെങ്കിലും ഉപകരണങ്ങൾ നിർമ്മിച്ച ഹോമിനിനുകൾ ജീവിച്ചിരുന്നു—ഒരുപക്ഷേ അതിലും വളരെ മുമ്പ് മുതൽ—എന്ന് കാണിക്കുന്നു.

thumbnail.alt: അഷ്യൂലിയൻ കൈക്കോടാലികളുടെ വിവിധ രൂപങ്ങൾ കാണിക്കുന്ന ചരിത്രചിത്രം

title: അത്തിരമ്പാക്കത്തിൽ 3,85,000 വർഷം മുമ്പുണ്ടായ സാങ്കേതിക മാറ്റം
excerpt: അത്തിരമ്പാക്കത്തിലെ താരതമ്യേന പുതിയ പാളികൾ അഷ്യൂലിയൻ കൈക്കോടാലികളുടെ ഉപയോഗം കുറഞ്ഞതും ഏകദേശം 3,85,000 വർഷം മുമ്പ് ആരംഭിച്ച ആദ്യകാല മധ്യ പുരാതന ശിലായുഗ ഉപകരണസമുച്ചയവും രേഖപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു.

thumbnail.alt: അത്തിരമ്പാക്കത്തിൽ നിന്നുള്ള ചെറിയ മുനയുള്ളതും ചീളെടുത്തതുമായ ശിലായുധങ്ങളുടെ ശേഖരം

title: Bairat Edict: Texts for the Buddhist community
excerpt: Ashoka recommends named Buddhist teachings to monks, nuns, and lay followers.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Bairat in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Ashoka’s edicts and inscriptions: a guide to the surviving texts
excerpt: Browse Ashoka’s rock, pillar, cave, Greek, and Aramaic inscriptions. Each distinct text has its own article with an image, transliteration, translation, and explanation.

title: Kandahar III: An Aramaic fragment of Pillar Edict VII
excerpt: Seven damaged lines from Kandahar preserve Indian phrases and Aramaic explanations that correspond to Ashoka’s seventh major pillar edict.

thumbnail.alt: Seven-line transcription of the damaged Kandahar III Aramaic inscription

title: Kandahar bilingual inscription: Piety and truth
excerpt: A Greek and Aramaic proclamation from Kandahar links the king’s moral policy with restraint, protection of living beings, and respect for parents.

thumbnail.alt: Kandahar rock inscription with Greek lines above Aramaic lines

title: Kandahar Greek inscription: Speech, Kalinga, and remorse
excerpt: A damaged Greek version of the ends of Major Rock Edicts XII and XIII urges restraint in speech and recounts the suffering caused by the conquest of Kalinga.

thumbnail.alt: Fragment of Ashoka’s Greek inscription from Kandahar

title: Karna Chaupar Cave inscription: Shelter for the rainy season
excerpt: A damaged Barabar inscription records a cave gift in Ashoka’s nineteenth regnal year.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi facsimiles of the three Barabar cave inscriptions in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition; Karna Chaupar is third

title: Laghman I: An Aramaic inscription associated with Priyadarśin
excerpt: A short Aramaic rock inscription names King Priyadarśin and gives disputed directions and distances. Its status as a royal edict remains uncertain.

thumbnail.alt: Six-line Aramaic inscription on rock at Laghman

title: Lumbini Pillar Edict: The Buddha’s birthplace
excerpt: Ashoka records a visit to Lumbini and favorable tax treatment for the village where the Buddha was born.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Lumbini in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict I: The rule of dhamma
excerpt: Ashoka says moral rule requires effort, self-examination, and concern for this life and the next.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict II: What dhamma means
excerpt: The king defines dhamma through compassion, generosity, truthfulness, purity, and avoiding wrongdoing.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict III: Examine your own faults
excerpt: Ashoka urges people to notice their own anger, cruelty, pride, and envy as well as their good actions.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict IV: Justice and the rajukas
excerpt: The king grants local officers authority while asking them to administer justice with fairness and restraint.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict V: Protection of animals
excerpt: Ashoka names protected animals and limits slaughter, branding, and fishing on specified days.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict VI: Edicts for public welfare
excerpt: The king reviews earlier inscriptions and says instructions on dhamma should be made known to all communities.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Pillar Edict VII: A royal review of dhamma
excerpt: Ashoka reviews his policies on welfare, religious respect, officers, public works, and persuasion.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Delhi–Topra in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict X: Fame is not enough
excerpt: Ashoka says renown matters only when it helps people follow dhamma.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Kalsi in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict XI: The gift of dhamma
excerpt: The king calls ethical conduct the highest kind of gift and social bond.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict XII: Restraint in religious speech
excerpt: Ashoka honors different religious groups and urges people to avoid careless attacks on other traditions.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict XIII: After the conquest of Kalinga
excerpt: Ashoka describes the suffering caused by the conquest of Kalinga and praises conquest by dhamma.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Kalsi in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict XIV: Why the edicts differ
excerpt: The king explains why inscriptions vary in length and wording from place to place.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict II: Care for people and animals
excerpt: The king describes medical treatment, useful plants, wells, and roadside trees for people and animals.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict III: Five-year tours of instruction
excerpt: Officials are ordered to travel every five years and teach conduct toward parents, others, and living beings.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict IV: The sound of dhamma
excerpt: Ashoka contrasts violence and the old drum of war with the public spread of dhamma.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict V: Officers of dhamma
excerpt: Ashoka describes appointing dhamma-mahamatras to work across religious groups and among vulnerable people.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Kalsi in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict VI: Reports at every hour
excerpt: Ashoka says officials may report the people’s affairs to him wherever he is and at any time.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict VII: All religious groups
excerpt: The king says members of all religious groups should be able to live throughout his realm.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict VIII: Journeys for dhamma
excerpt: Ashoka replaces royal pleasure tours with journeys involving gifts, visits to elders, and moral discussion.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Girnar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Major Rock Edict IX: Rituals and moral practice
excerpt: The king questions customary ceremonies and recommends the continuing practice of dhamma instead.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Kalsi in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Minor Rock Edict I: Ashoka’s effort
excerpt: Ashoka describes his commitment as a Buddhist lay follower and urges people of every rank to work earnestly.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Rūpnāth in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Minor Rock Edict II: Everyday duties
excerpt: The king urges obedience to parents and elders, truthfulness, and gentle treatment of living beings.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Brahmagiri in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Nigali Sagar Pillar Edict: The Konakamana stupa
excerpt: Ashoka records enlarging a stupa for the Buddha Konakamana and later visiting the site.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Nigali Sagar in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Pul-i Darunta: An Aramaic and Prakrit inscription
excerpt: An eight-line fragment from near Laghman combines Middle Indian phrases with Aramaic explanations and refers to several of Ashoka’s edicts.

thumbnail.alt: Line tracing of eight surviving Aramaic-script lines from the Pul-i Darunta inscription

title: Queen’s Edict: Gifts of Karuvaki
excerpt: Ashoka orders donations by Queen Karuvaki to be recorded in her name.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Allahabad–Kauśāmbī in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Schism Edict: Unity of the Saṃgha
excerpt: Ashoka orders officials to act against monks or nuns who divide the Buddhist community.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Sarnath in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Separate Rock Edict I: Justice in Kalinga
excerpt: Ashoka instructs officials in newly conquered Kalinga to avoid arbitrary punishment and treat people fairly.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Dhauli in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Separate Rock Edict II: Trust on the frontier
excerpt: Ashoka tells Kalinga’s officials to reassure people beyond the border and govern with patience.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi inscription facsimile from Dhauli in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition

title: Sudama Cave inscription: A gift to the Ajivikas
excerpt: In his twelfth regnal year, Ashoka dedicates the Banyan Cave at Barabar to the Ajivikas.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi facsimiles of the three Barabar cave inscriptions in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition; Sudama is first

title: Taxila Aramaic inscription: A damaged mention of Priyadarśin
excerpt: A broken Aramaic inscription from Taxila mentions Priyadarśin twice, but its missing text leaves its message and royal authorship uncertain.

thumbnail.alt: Damaged Aramaic writing on the surviving Taxila stone fragment

title: Visvakarma Cave inscription: A second Ajivika gift
excerpt: Ashoka dedicates a cave on the Khalatika mountain to the Ajivikas in his twelfth regnal year.

thumbnail.alt: Brahmi facsimiles of the three Barabar cave inscriptions in Hultzsch’s 1925 edition; Visvakarma is second
